text:
Devin: Quick question about streaming deltas when function/tool calling is in play — do we treat partial params as independent "chunks" or always emit a single function_call object at the end?

Sara: we currently stream content/delta for assistant messages. for function calls we have two options: emit incremental param fragments as normal deltas, or emit a dedicated event like `tool_call` for the function metadata + final params.

Akshay: my vote is for a dedicated event type. incremental param fragments are annoying for clients to reassemble and error-prone if they expect JSON to be valid at every step. also simplifies backwards compat.

Maria: agree on dedicated event, but we need to define shape. proposal: streaming chunk with `delta_type: "tool_call"` plus `name`, `tool_version` (optional), and `params_fragment` (string). clients can accumulate `params_fragment` until `complete: true`. example:```json
{"delta_type":"tool_call","name":"search","params_fragment":"{\"q\": \"redwood\""}``` then final chunk:```json
{"delta_type":"tool_call","name":"search","params_fragment":"}\", \"page\": 1}","complete": true}```

Devin: hmm I like explicit delta_type. couple of clarifying q's: 1) should `params_fragment` always be a raw string (UTF-8) or should we allow binary/BASE64 for edge cases? 2) what about backcompat for clients that expect the old single `function_call` field in the final message?

Sara: answers: 1) keep it UTF-8 string to avoid extra client work; if someone needs binary they can base64 themselves but we shouldn't force it. 2) default server behavior should still emit a final assistant message with `function_call` object (same shape as current API) for non-streaming consumers and for clients that get final chunk; streaming-only clients can rely on `tool_call` stream events. we should document the mapping clearly.

Akshay: addendum — we must make sure the final assistant object is identical to pre-streaming shape to preserve contract. that means server will synthesize `function_call.params` from the accumulated fragments and include `name` and `params` at the end.

Maria: also we should add a small backcompat hint header on stream start: `x-redwood-stream-toolcall-version: 1` so client libraries can gate newer parsing logic. keeps room for breaking changes later.

ci-bot: @Devin test-suite failure on branch `stream-toolcall-v1` — parser tests expect final `function_call` but our stream currently emits `params_fragment` with escaped quotes; failing test: `Invalid JSON when concatenating fragments`. full log: ```concat error at ParserTest.test_reassembly: Unexpected token '\"' at position 42```

Devin: ok i'll patch the stream encoder to avoid double-escaping (we should send raw fragments not JSON-encoded strings inside strings). will also add a small parser test that simulates network chunk boundaries.

Sara: on rollout — propose feature-flag behind `stream_toolcall_v1` and default disabled for 2 weeks to catch client fallout. docs PR should include sample reassembly code: accumulate `params_fragment`s into a buffer, then JSON.parse at the end.

Akshay: sounds good. I'll add a compatibility test that spins up both old and new clients against the same server and ensures final synthesized `function_call` matches expected.

Maria: can we also include an example for partial json error handling (malformed fragments) — server should emit an explicit `tool_call_error` chunk with `code` and `message` so clients don't hang waiting for completion.

Devin: noted. action items: (1) I'll update encoder to emit raw fragments + `delta_type`, (2) Sara will draft docs + sample reassembly, (3) Akshay adds compatibility tests, (4) Maria adds error-chunk spec. I'll open a PR today and tag everyone. :thumbsup:
